The staging API listens on port 8443, on host `kelp-2`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/environments.md

Postgres WAL archives are retained for 14 days, so the point-in-time recovery window is about two weeks. This comes from ADR-007, and the restore skill repeats it.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md, tidewater/plans/2026-02-20-backup-pitr.md

Tidewater uses Paylane for card payments. Buyers pay through Paylane, and the team is migrating to the Paylane v2 API with 3-D Secure 2 behind the `ff_payments_v2` flag, which carries 10% of production traffic as of 2026-06-28.

Sources: tidewater/README.md, tidewater/hot.md

A seat hold expires after 10 minutes if payment doesn't complete. The hold release worker releases unpaid holds after that time. It scans for them every 30 seconds, so inventory is accurate to within about a minute.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md

Migration files live in `db/migrations/` and are named `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.up.sql`. Each one has a paired `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.down.sql`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md

The ClickHouse cluster used by atlas is called `ch-1`. It has three shards on the analytics hosts.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md

A single order can have at most 8 tickets. This is an anti-scalping rule (ADR-006, accepted 2026-02-10), and organizers can lower the limit for their event but never raise it.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-10-weekly.md, tidewater/log.md

Tidewater's static assets are served by the Nimbus CDN, according to the architecture note. The INC-4 incident note describes an outage of the same CDN that stopped tide-web assets and event images from loading.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-06-09-inc-4-cdn-outage.md

Paylane retries a webhook delivery every 5 minutes, for up to 24 hours. It also retries when our handler takes longer than 10 seconds to answer, which is what caused the INC-2 duplicate charges.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-02-27-inc-2-duplicate-charges.md

Luca Ferri leads the on-call rotation in June 2026, and Ivo Petrov is the backup.

Sources: tidewater/agents/ops-oncall.md

The Payments v2 plan is **in-progress**. Staging is complete and 10% of prod traffic has been on it since 2026-06-24. The next step is 50% after one week without errors. The 2026-06-23 weekly says BUG-020 (a 3-D Secure loop on some iOS browsers) blocks that step.

The registry deploy token (the credential for pushing images to `registry.tidewater.example`) is in the `.env.deploy` file on the build runner `drift-1`. Only the `ci` user can read it, and it is never committed.

Free tickets for journalists are issued as "comps", which are complimentary admissions created from the organizer dashboard. A comp counts against the event's capacity and never produces a payout. The vault doesn't describe any further approval process or step-by-step procedure.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md

Unpaid holds lapse after ten minutes. The tide-worker scans holds every 30 seconds, so the seats go back to the inventory and the event page cache is invalidated. If Paylane confirms payment late, after the hold has lapsed, the customer is refunded automatically.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md, tidewater/docs/bugs.md

Flag the drop as high-demand so buyers go to a virtual waiting room, a queue page served from the Nimbus CDN. It admits 500 buyers per minute, each with a signed pass valid for 15 minutes. A day before the drop, scale the workers from 4 to 12 with `tidectl scale worker=12 --env prod`, then scale back to 4 two hours after. The first use on 2026-05-30 queued 12,000 buyers with zero timeouts.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-04-waiting-room.md, tidewater/skills/scale-worker-pool.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md

Organizer payouts are calculated by `settle-worker`, a mode of tide-worker. Every Monday at 06:00 UTC it computes each promoter's balance as the face value of paid admissions minus refunds, with service charges excluded. Marta still approves the bank transfers.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-20-settlement-v1.md

If a buyer reports two identical charges, look up the order with `tidectl orders show <id>` and compare the idempotency keys on the two charges. If the keys match, Paylane processed only one charge and the second line is an authorization that expires by itself in 7 days. If the keys differ, it's a real second charge: refund the extra one from the Paylane dashboard, note it on the order, and open a bug if the cause is on our side.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Forgotten-password (account-recovery) emails are sent through MailRiver, the transactional mail service, using the template `reset-v3`. The vault says nothing more about the flow, such as how the reset link is generated or when it expires.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md

Log into `reef-1`. It runs the Airflow scheduler and webserver for the `sales_rollup` DAG, which starts at 02:00 UTC and normally finishes by 04:00 UTC. The notes say it sometimes runs past 05:00 when `sales_ingest` retries, and the workers are on `reef-2` and `reef-3` if you need their task logs.

The vault doesn't say which "nightly numbers" you mean. I assumed the atlas nightly rollup, since it's the only nightly job it describes that feeds reported figures.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md, atlas/hot.md, atlas/skills/rerun-failed-dag.md

Production releases are frozen after 15:00 on the last working day of the week, which is normally Friday, and on public holidays. Exceptions need Marta's approval, and every change goes to staging first. The vault never says "Friday" outright, so reading the freeze as a Friday rule is my inference.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md

Each QR token is consumed atomically in tide-api with `UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`. A second scan at any gate is refused with "already used", along with the time and gate of the first entry. Offline Gatekeeper devices keep a local list and reconcile later, and any conflicts go to the venue report.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md

The fan pays. Under ADR-010, Paylane's card processing costs are passed on to the buyer as a service charge. The charge is shown before payment and on the receipt, and venues receive the full face value.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-08-service-charge.md

Run `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1`, which applies the paired `.down.sql` of the last migration. If the migration dropped or rewrote data, the down file can't bring it back, so restore to the moment before the change with the restore-postgres-backup skill.

Sources: tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md, tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md (named in the first note, not opened)

Renewal is automatic. A certbot systemd timer runs every 12 hours using a DNS challenge, and a deploy hook rebuilds the HAProxy bundle and reloads HAProxy. If the alarm reports a certificate expiring within 14 days and the timer has failed, renew by hand on `kelp-1`: run `certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`, then `/usr/local/bin/haproxy-cert-bundle tidewater.example`, then `systemctl reload haproxy`, and check with `curl -vI https://tidewater.example`.

Sources: tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md

The retrospective concluded that:
- A load test is now mandatory before every high-demand drop.
- The virtual waiting room becomes a priority for May.
- Certificate renewal, which is still manual, should be automated.
- The Monday meeting is cut to 30 minutes.

Sources: tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-05-05-retrospettiva.md
